body:
**Momentum and related anomalies**
- Jegadeesh & Titman (1993): buying past 3-12-month winners and selling losers earned ~1% per month over the following 3-12 months (US, 1965-1989); profits partly reverse after 1-2 years. — [Journal of Finance, DOI 10.1111/j.1540-6261.1993.tb04702.x](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.1993.tb04702.x) [K]
- Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), "Time series momentum": a security's own past 12-month return predicts its future return across futures/forwards in equity indices, currencies, commodities and bonds; partial reversal at longer horizons; diversified TSMOM performs best in extreme markets. — [JFE 104(2):228-250](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfineco.2011.11.003) [F for citation; 58-instrument count not verified]
- George & Hwang (2004): nearness of price to the 52-week high explains a large portion of momentum profits and dominates past-return-based momentum in forecasting; returns do not reverse in the long run. Later work finds 52-week-high profits in 18 of 20 international markets. — [Journal of Finance 59(5):2145-2176](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.2004.00695.x) [F]; [CXO Advisory summary](https://www.cxoadvisory.com/1284/technical-trading/the-52-week-high-as-a-momentum-indicator-for-individual-stocks/) [F]
- Post-earnings-announcement drift (Bernard & Thomas 1989): stocks with the most positive earnings surprises continue to drift up for ~60 trading days after the announcement (and negative surprises drift down) — supports CAN SLIM "C" and Qullamaggie EPs. — [Journal of Accounting Research 27, DOI 10.2307/2491062](https://doi.org/10.2307/2491062) [K]
- Momentum crashes (Daniel & Moskowitz 2016): momentum suffers rare, severe crashes, typically in "panic states" right after market declines when the market rebounds sharply — the risk practitioners' market-regime filters try to manage. — [JFE 122(2), DOI 10.1016/j.jfineco.2015.12.002](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfineco.2015.12.002) [K]
- India: momentum profits documented and not explained by CAPM/FF3, concentrated in winners. — [Ansari & Khan 2012](https://emerald.com/insight/content/doi/10.1108/03074351211193730/full/html) [F]; [Maheshwari & Dhankar 2017](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:eme:jamrpp:jamr-11-2015-0081) [F]

The "₹5,000" figure is literally true as seed capital but misleading: the Tata Tea trade alone needed more than 40x that.
- The 2-3% initial sizing quote contrasts with his eventual Titan concentration. He built conviction positions over time, adding as the thesis played out and letting winners run, rather than starting big.

`strategy:soros-reflexivity` | confidence: **single-source** | tags: global, process, macro, cyclical

Reflexivity: participants' beliefs change the fundamentals they are trying to price. Typical boom-bust sequence (Soros, Alchemy of Finance): (1) an unrecognised trend begins; (2) a prevailing bias forms and reinforces it - rising prices ease financing (equity issuance, collateral-backed credit), which lifts reported growth; (3) tests survive, conviction grows; (4) a divergence opens between belief and reality; (5) a twilight period where the trend continues on momentum but doubts grow; (6) a crossover and accelerating reversal. Indian examples: 2003-08 infra/realty (rising land values -> bigger loans -> more projects -> higher valuations -> QIPs), 2023-24 PSU rerating (rising prices -> retail and MF inflows -> more buying), 2024 SME IPOs (oversubscription -> listing gains -> more applicants). Rules for individuals: identify the feedback loop and its fuel (credit, IPO funding, retail flows); ride early only with small size; watch the fuel - when financing tightens (RBI/SEBI action, funding costs, lock-up expiries, promoter selling) the loop breaks. Risk: timing is hard; many 'bubbles' run far longer than expected.

Links: person:george-soros (about); case_study:india-bull-2003-08 (illustrates)

Sources: <https://www.wikipedia.com/wiki/Soros_Fund> ; <https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Quantum_Fund>

`case_study:hal-2020-2024` · tickers: HAL, BEL · confidence: verified

IPO Mar 2018 at ₹1,215 (≈₹607 after the 2023 1:2 split). IPO buyers then fell −56% to ₹251 (May 2020) and waited about three years to break even. From ₹251 → ATH ₹5,552 (Jul 2024) ≈22x: trailing P/E 6.3 → 48.7 (7.7x) × implied EPS ~2.9x, so about 66% of the log-return was rerating. Drawdowns: −47% (Aug–Oct 2020), −44% (Jul 2024–Feb 2025). ₹4,760 on 19 Nov 2026 (−14%); EPS kept rising (FY24 ₹114 → TTM ₹143), so P/E is ~33. Early signal: in 2020 it was a monopoly military-aircraft maker at 6–11x P/E with OPM rising from 15% to 25%. On 13 Jan 2021 the CCS cleared and on 3 Feb 2021 the government signed a ₹48k cr (₹45,696 cr + infrastructure) contract for 83 Tejas Mk1A, a public, multi-year revenue signal. Margins then reached ~30%. The Motilal Oswal 2020–25 wealth-creation study ranked HAL the most consistent and best all-round wealth creator. Companion BEL: ₹19.9 (May 2020) → ₹468 (Mar 2026) ≈23.5x, EPS ~5.2x, P/E 12.8 → 57. Lesson: the policy plus a single-digit-P/E monopoly drove the rerating, while continuing EPS growth (unlike the shipyards) kept the drawdown after the peak moderate.

Key data: **start_year**: 2020; **end_year**: 2024; **start_price**: 251; **end_price**: 5552; **price_nov2026**: 4760; **multiple**: ~22x (BEL ~23.5x); **pe_start**: 6.3; **pe_end**: 48.7; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~2.9x; **max_drawdown**: -56% post-IPO 2018-20; -47% 2020; **early_signals**: 6x P/E monopoly; Tejas contract Feb 2021; **ended**: not ended; P/E normalised 49→33 with EPS growth; **lesson**: rerating + continuing EPS holds; IPO buyers needed patience

Sources: <https://www.screener.in/company/HAL/consolidated/> · <https://www.screener.in/company/BEL/consolidated/> · <https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1694844> · <https://theprint.in/defence/govt-clears-rs-48000-cr-deal-for-83-tejas-mk-1a-all-you-want-to-know-about-the-aircraft/584743> · <https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/top-wealth-creators-of-2020-25-biggest-fastest-and-consistent-firms-here-125121200301_1.html>

`thesis:paper-call:US-FIVE:fy2026-comps-11pct-plus` (made 2026-11-21, P = 0.58, base 0.50). Facts its reasoning did **not** use, recorded for the post-mortem:
- **What the guide implies.** H1 FY26 comps were +18.3%; Q3 is guided +8–10%. Management says the FY guide of +10–12% **implies Q4 ≈ +3%** `[CC-Q2FY26, single-source]`.
- **My comp-base weighting.** Weights from FY25 quarterly sales: H1 41.6%, Q3 21.8%, Q4 36.3% [EST]. On these, FY ≥ 11.0% needs Q4 ≥ ~4% if Q3 lands at +9%, and **Q4 ≥ ~1% if Q3 repeats the beat pattern (~+14%)**.
- **For YES:** 5 for 5 quarterly beats of +4.4 to +8.4 pp; the Q3 results (~early Dec) arrive before resolution; holiday merchandise newness.
- **For NO:** Q4 laps +15.4%; an "unfavorable shrink comparison" (a margin item, not comps); fuel; consumer softening; and the CFO explicitly calls the guide "thoughtful", not conservative.
- **Net:** the call's main premise (beat-and-raise means a conservative H2) is supported by the promise tracker in §7.2. The weighting shows the threshold is low *if* Q3 beats. **Lesson for the paper-call method:** compute the implied remaining-quarter comp from the FY guide before setting a probability.

- **What the market appears to price:** peak earnings that will fall after the April-2027 pre-buy (P/E 12.9 on peak EPS, ~26x normalised).
- **Our view:** *no claimable mispricing; we agree with the market's direction.* We add two things it may under-weight: (1) the like-for-like
  revenue lag in FY26 (content/share per vehicle not growing) and (2) an annually renewable 4.5%-of-sales parent fee that minorities cannot vote on.
  Positive offset: net cash 15% of market cap and through-cycle ROIC ~15%, so the left tail is a cyclical drawdown (FY19–21 type), not ruin.
- **What would prove us wrong:** FY27 revenue ≥ ₹2,500 cr *and* H1 FY28 revenue within 10% of H1 FY27 (cycle longer than assumed); fee stable or
  lower on a multi-year agreement; FY27 revenue growth ≥ industry + 5 pts (content story real).
- **Base-class departure (card §5):** P(≥3x) 6% vs 21% class — a 3x from a peak-EPS base needs ~25% EPS CAGR at a 26x exit (twin engine); the
  peak-to-peak record is 4.4%. Tails anchored at w = 0.6 (above the 0.5 default) because this stock printed a ~0.20x drawdown in the last cycle.

| Capital allocation | No debt; cash 16% of mcap earning ~6%; payout 20–40%; no expansion capex (single leased site) | Conservative; cash piling up — possibly a buffer for the dispute |
| Who takes value before minorities? | Apollo (pharmacy margin, services ~5.6% of revenue); GNCTD (free-treatment claim) | **Both partners**; the JV contract has lapsed |
| Fraud / solvency trap? | Clean audit, no debt, no pledge | **No** |
**Conclusion:** cheap because a **verified legal cause** (expired lease, hostile government affidavit, SC warning) can remove the operating
business; it is a **legal-option value trap, not a fraud, solvency or cycle trap**. As with SUNFLAG (L33), a discount with verified causes is not a
claimable edge.

FY26 from XBRL = AR: revenue 2,368.26; materials 1,347.76 − inventory change 27.99 (+ contract-manufacturing COGS 60.30, tagged inside
"OtherExpenses" in FY26/FY27 XBRL but inside materials in FY25 — a tagging change); employees 360.56; other expenses 385.83; finance 55.51;
D&A 119.37; PBT before exceptional 76.49; exceptional +35.92; PAT 69.15; EPS 5.00 — = screener ✓.
- **Core vs reported (the key L2 finding).** TTM PBT 159.4 includes **exceptional +63.0** (fire-insurance realisations: 33.07 in Q3
  FY26, 29.95 in Q1 FY27) and other income 12.1 → **core PBT ~₹84 cr** `[XBRL]`. Core EPS **₹3.4–3.9** by three routes (EBIT 145.2 ×
  0.65 − post-tax interest 45.8 = ₹3.51; PBT ex-exceptional less tax = ₹3.42; screener's ex-exceptional P/E 32.5 ⇒ ₹3.9) → **P/E ~33–37x,
  not 18.7x**. Effective tax is high (38% FY26; ~51% on TTM core) because European/US losses carry no tax shield.
- **Fire (23-Apr-2024, Vashivali, Raigad):** loss ₹60.55 cr net of an interim insurance relief of ₹95 cr (FY25 exceptional); FY26
  realised ₹35.46 cr more; Q1 FY27 ₹30 cr more `[AR26 n.48; CALL Aug-2026]`. Insurance premium 6.1 → 20.8 cr (+0.6 pp of sales) since.
- **Group ROIC/ROIIC first (L42) [EST].** Invested capital Sep-2026 = equity 1,420.7 + net debt 910.7 = **₹2,331 cr** (incl. goodwill
  360 + other intangibles 162). TTM NOPAT 145.2 × 0.70 = 101.6 → **ROIC 4.4%**; adding back management's ₹80 cr creative-centre opex
  ("deduct Rs.80 crore and add it to the profitability" `[CALL Q2]`) → 6.8%. **Full-cycle window** FY17–19 → FY24–26 (no trough-to-peak):
  avg EBIT ex OI 131 → 181 on avg IC ~1,040 → ~2,124 (equity + screener borrowings) → ROIC 8.8% → 6.0%, **ROIIC ~3%**. Segment view: Flavours
  27% pre-tax on segment assets, Fragrance 6.0% — the Fragrance segment carries the European acquisitions and centres. CEO: India ROCE
  "in 20% range"; centres need "three to four years before we are breakeven… seven, eight years… a good return" `[CALL Q2]`.
- **Normalised EPS (v1.4):** mean EPS FY17–26 = **₹6.69 → 19.1x** vs 18.7x reported trailing and ~36x core. Here trailing and normalised
  agree, and the misleading number is the *trailing* one (inflated by insurance) — the cyclicals rule alone would have missed this.
- **Ten-year compounding:** EPS FY16 ₹5.05 → FY26 ₹5.00 (≈0%/yr) while revenue grew 9.9%/yr and invested capital ~2.6x.
